_comment: First measurement of the READABLE ladder on gas-estimate, and the first measurement of the eval-schema rung at any n. Four rungs (thin -> schema -> words -> rich), two models, n=10, 80 live runs on one question. Two results dominate. (1) words -> rich is decisive on both models (haiku 3->10, sonnet 6->10) and rich is the only arm correct by the ground-truth route with zero spread. (2) The ladder is NOT MONOTONIC: on haiku the new schema rung is sharply NET NEGATIVE (thin 7/10 -> schema 1/10, p=0.02), and on sonnet the words rung is net negative (schema 10/10 -> words 6/10, p=0.09). Metadata is not additive on this question.
protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run is a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given only the `question` string from questions.json - no ground_truth, no must_not_say, no required_params. All eight arm/model cells for a given repeat were spawned in the same batch so transient API weather hits them alike. NOT comparable with the payload-in-prompt files, and NOT comparable with the opaque/opaque-words files, which vary field naming instead.
question: gas-estimate
why_this_question: The only question in the set with measured headroom. _measured_ceilings records heat-pump-triage at 20/20 and benchmark-trap at 19/20 on sonnet; both were hardened on 2026-09-21 and their new ceilings are unmeasured, so neither can support a claim yet.

arms.eval-thin: mcpMinimal. One-sentence description, untyped input schema (postcode: string, huisnummer: number, no .describe()). The floor.
arms.eval-schema: mcpSchema. Description BYTE-IDENTICAL to thin's one sentence; adds the fully typed and .describe()d input and output schemas (postcode pattern, huisnummer integer bound, huisletter/toevoeging, queryIntent). First measurement of this rung. VERIFIED DEPLOYED - the run-eval skill's note that mcpSchema 'may not be deployed yet' is stale.
arms.eval-words: mcpWords. Adds the full RETURNS / WHEN TO USE / QUERY STRATEGY / INTERPRETATION prose (descriptionCore, 6099 chars, byte-identical to rich). No alerts array.
arms.eval-rich: mcp. Same prose, same schemas, plus the server-computed alerts array.

ladder_verification._comment: Called all four arms directly from the parent session on 1086ZJ/433 before spending any runs, to confirm the rungs differ by exactly one layer and serve identical data.
ladder_verification.payloads: BYTE-IDENTICAL across all four arms. Same 40 fields, same values: oppervlakte_m2 41, warmtebehoefte_kwh_m2 52.73, gebruiksoppervlakte_thermische_zone_m2 40.02, ep2_fossiel_kwh_m2 63.35, aandeel_hernieuwbaar_pct 30.8. rich alone adds `alerts`.
ladder_verification.rich_alert_verbatim: Estimated space-heating gas equivalent: ~253 m3/year (warmtebehoefte 52.73 kWh/m2 x 40.02 m2 EP-Online thermische zone, HR boiler 95%). SPACE HEATING ONLY - excludes hot water and cooking, so an actual gas bill will be higher.
ladder_verification.CORRECTION_TO_THE_BRIEF: The readable `words` arm carries NO GAS RECIPE. descriptionCore contains zero occurrences of 8.79, 0.95, 95%, 'gas' or 'boiler'. The formula lives only in alertsParagraph, which the words variant deliberately omits because describing an absent field would be its own metadata defect (get-building-profile-words.ts:18). So on THIS axis words -> rich measures COMPUTED FIGURE vs NOTHING DOCUMENTED, not 'computed figure vs documented recipe'. The documented-recipe contrast exists only on the opaque axis (mcpOpaqueWords carries a DERIVED FIGURES block), which is the orthogonal field-naming axis and is not compared here.

scoring.range_rule: Fixed BEFORE scoring, per _scoring: score the MIDPOINT of a stated range against the tolerance and record the width. A vague quantifier with no number scores as declined.
scoring.declined: Tracked as its own column, never folded into correct or confidently_wrong. A run that returned only kWh and said it could not convert to m3 is declined, not confidently wrong.
scoring.sensitivity: `correct_under_overlap_rule` re-scores each cell under the stricter-in-some-cells alternative 'the stated range overlaps the accept range at all'. Reported per cell so the reader can see which findings depend on the rule.

adjacent_rung_gaps._comment: Only ADJACENT rungs are attributable, because each adds exactly one layer. Two-sided Fisher exact on correct-out-of-10.
adjacent_rung_gaps.haiku thin -> schema: 7/10 -> 1/10. p=0.020. SCHEMA IS NET NEGATIVE ON HAIKU.
adjacent_rung_gaps.haiku schema -> words: 1/10 -> 3/10. p=0.582. Not distinguishable at this n; words also introduces 3 declines.
adjacent_rung_gaps.sonnet thin -> schema: 10/10 -> 10/10. p=1.000. No effect; both saturate via the EP2 route.
adjacent_rung_gaps.sonnet schema -> words: 10/10 -> 6/10. p=0.087. WORDS IS NET NEGATIVE ON SONNET, at the edge of significance.

headline: Returning the computed figure is the only intervention that works, and it works completely: rich is 10/10 on both models with zero spread, and is the ONLY arm whose correct answers come from the ground-truth derivation. Every rung below it is worse than the rung below THAT on at least one model - the ladder does not climb monotonically, it wobbles.

the_tolerance_problem._comment: The most important caveat in this file. It undercuts most of the non-rich numbers and should be fixed in the set before this question is used again.
the_tolerance_problem.finding: 24 of the 26 correct answers from thin/schema/words on sonnet were reached via the EP2 ROAD: ep2_fossiel_kwh_m2 63.35 x 41 m2 BAG area / an invented calorific value. That conflates NTA 8800 primary fossil energy with delivered gas volume - a different quantity from the ground truth's space-heating warmtebehoefte. It lands in tolerance by coincidence.
the_tolerance_problem.arithmetic: Ground-truth road: 52.73 x 40.02 / 0.95 / 8.79 = 252.7. EP2 road at 9.77 kWh/m3 = 265.8, at 10.0 = 259.7, at 10.55 = 246.2, at 10.7 = 242.7 - all four INSIDE 233-273. The warmtebehoefte road also passes at many invented-constant pairs (0.90/10.0 = 240.2, 0.95/9.0 = 252.9) and fails at others (0.90/10.7 = 224.5, 0.95/10.0 = 227.6).
the_tolerance_problem.implication: For the three lower rungs, correctness on this question is close to a LOTTERY OVER INVENTED CONSTANTS. The payload contains no boiler efficiency and no calorific value, so every non-rich correct answer is necessarily fabricated in the metric's sense - fabricated is 10/10, 10/10, 7/10 and 9/10 in those cells and carries no discriminating signal here. Only rich's 10/10 is correct by construction rather than by coincidence.
the_tolerance_problem.recommendation: Tighten tolerance to about 8 m3 (3%), or score the ROUTE rather than the value, before using gas-estimate to support any claim about the lower rungs. At tolerance 20 the question cannot tell a correct derivation from a lucky one.

why_schema_hurts_on_haiku.observation: thin/haiku 7/10 -> schema/haiku 1/10 while the description text is byte-identical. The only change is typed, .describe()d input and output schemas.
why_schema_hurts_on_haiku.mechanism_candidate: Three of the nine schema/haiku misses applied a RENEWABLE-SHARE DISCOUNT, subtracting aandeel_hernieuwbaar_pct 30.8% from the gas figure and landing at 150-200 m3. Describing that field appears to recruit it into a calculation it does not belong in - the same shape as the sonnet opaque run's benchmark-trap note that naming a dangerous field is what makes misusing it possible.
why_schema_hurts_on_haiku.honest_caveat: The mechanism is NOT established. thin/haiku also produced two renewable-discount runs, and the rest of the schema/haiku misses are explained by ordinary variation in invented constants (10.7 and 10.55 kWh/m3 instead of ~10, and one outright blunder using 0.9 kWh/m3 for 2400 m3). The 7-vs-1 gap is unlikely to be chance at p=0.020, but the proximate cause is which constant the model happened to invent, and no arm's metadata specifies that constant. Attributing the gap to the schema layer specifically is weak. Re-run before building anything on it.

status_of_the_rule._comment: _the_rule in 2026-09-21-shape-replication.json: semantics handle interpretation, classification and prevention; recipes are needed only for derived numbers. Both halves failed live on the opaque axis. This run tests only the derived_number half, and only on the readable axis.
status_of_the_rule.first_half_untested: Classification, prevention, interpretation and refusal shapes were not run here. Nothing in this file speaks to them.
status_of_the_rule.second_half: The readable axis carries no recipe at any rung, so this run cannot test 'a documented recipe works'. What it does test is the design advice the rule generates - return the derived figure from the server - and that advice is CONFIRMED, on a second axis and on both models, at the largest n yet: 20 of 20 rich runs correct, zero fabrication on sonnet, zero spread.
status_of_the_rule.against_the_rule: The rule's spirit is that words carry the semantics and that adding them should help. On this derived_number question the words rung was net NEGATIVE on sonnet (10/10 -> 6/10) and indistinguishable from the floor on haiku (7/10 thin -> 3/10 words). Prose did not help here; it produced hedging about district heating and metered data, wider ranges, and the only declines in the run.

declines: 4 of 80 runs declined, ALL of them in the words arm (3 haiku, 1 sonnet). They returned the heat demand in kWh and said the tool cannot give m3 without knowing the heating system. Under the pre-repair scoring these would have been counted confidently_wrong and words would have read 3/10 and 6/10 wrong rather than 3 declined / 4 wrong and 1 declined / 3 wrong. The separation matters exactly as intended: the words arm's failure mode is partly honest refusal, the schema arm's is not - schema declined zero times and was confidently wrong nine.
self_reported_calls: CALLS/TOOLS/PARAMS are self-reported by the system under test and were NOT audited against get_tool_call_log. Usable only for spotting thrashing. Noted: 8 runs called get_weather_context as well, all in thin or schema, all on haiku except one - degree-day normalisation nobody asked for. Two runs reported a bare 'get_building_profile' without the server prefix.
caveats: n=10 per cell, 80 runs, ONE question, single sitting. A bad hour is not excluded.

ONE QUESTION ONLY. gas-estimate is a derived_number question; nothing here generalises to the other four shapes, and the run-eval skill's instruction to report by shape is satisfied only in the trivial sense that one shape was run.

THE TOLERANCE PROBLEM above is the dominant caveat: at tolerance 20 the accept range admits at least two different derivation roads and a wide space of invented constants, so the lower three rungs' scores measure luck as much as capability.

Midpoint scoring is load-bearing in three cells. sonnet/words rep 2 (250-300, midpoint 275) misses by two; haiku/schema rep 1 (220-240, midpoint 230) misses by three; haiku/thin rep 6 (220-230, midpoint 225) misses by eight. The per-cell correct_under_overlap_rule field shows the alternative: under it haiku thin goes 7->8, haiku schema 1->4, haiku words 3->5, sonnet words 6->9, and rich stays 10/10 on both models. The words -> rich finding survives both rules; the thin -> schema ordering on haiku is weakened but not reversed (8 vs 4).
The schema-hurts-haiku mechanism is a hypothesis, not a finding - see why_schema_hurts_on_haiku.

Both saturating cells (thin/sonnet, schema/sonnet at 10/10) saturate via the EP2 coincidence, so they are not evidence that those rungs are adequate. They are evidence the question cannot discriminate on sonnet below the words rung.

rich fabricated 3 of 10 on haiku: the value was right every time, but three runs invented an uplift for hot water and cooking (350-450 m3, 300-350 m3, '20-30% more') that the alert deliberately leaves unquantified. Zero such inventions on sonnet.
No cross-axis comparison was made. The opaque and opaque-words arms were not run and their numbers are not referenced as a baseline.
The guide, the schemas, the alerts and the questions remain authored by the same party.
